analysis.title: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) 1QFY: At the center of 2027 enterprise deployments
key_insights: Microsoft reported 1QFY27 revenue of $92.3bn (+19% cc yoy), 2% above the Street, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 (+27% yoy), 3% above the Street. The stock was indicated +3% after hours.

GS says investor focus across the AI ecosystem has shifted in the last two weeks to the sustainability of token demand, token economics and mix, and the depth of the financing markets. GS argues Microsoft's enterprise AI strategy is working into 2027 in both apps and platform/infrastructure.
Copilot revenue growth accelerated qoq, daily users rose about 50% qoq, and customers consuming Copilot credits through usage-based billing rose 75%.

Foundry revenue grew more than 3x yoy and customers building agentic solutions across multiple models rose 5x. Use cases include automated order taking, inventory maintenance and end-to-end business processes. GS sees diffusion from experimentation to production as a primary growth driver in 2027.

Microsoft's model strategy has three prongs: use the latest frontier model, route dynamically across models on quality, speed and cost, or train proprietary models on customer traces, including with MAI. MAI is meant to expand the options offered, not displace frontier models.
Microsoft targets MAI capabilities comparable to leading frontier models within 3-6 months of release at a fraction of the training cost. Early MAI deployments span cyber, transcription and coding.

Azure grew 48% in 1Q. Microsoft guided to 49%-50% cc growth in 2Q despite a delay in 3P capacity shifting into 2H. Demand continues to exceed available supply and growth is broad based across enterprises and SMBs, core cloud and AI infrastructure.

Microsoft added 24 new data centers in 1QFY and cut dock-to-live times by about 20% qoq. Engineering improvements, including monetizing previously underutilized CPU capacity, created incremental capacity. Copilot throughput improved more than 50% qoq.
MAI 200 delivers up to 1.7x more tokens per watt across Teams and Copilot. MAI 300 is expected to deliver 40% more tokens per watt versus leading GPU-based systems.
GS raised its F27E/F28E/F29E revenue forecasts to $395bn/$488bn/$597bn from $389bn/$472bn/$570bn, and adjusted EPS to $19.73/$24.28/$29.87 from $19.21/$23.08/$27.87. It introduced F31E EPS of $46.77.
GS raised its 12-month price target to $700 from $640, based on an unchanged 28x P/E on SNTM adjusted net income. The rating is Buy (on the Conviction List), with 31.8% upside from $531.01.
Free cash flow excluding finance leases was $18.6bn (-27% yoy), below GSe of $20.4bn and well above the Street figure of $8.5bn. Capex was $45.2bn (+30% yoy), 13% below both GSe and the Street.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target to $700 from $640 on a 28x P/E applied to SNTM adjusted net income, after a 1QFY27 beat and higher estimates. The rating is Buy with the Conviction List designation (CL) and 31.8% upside.

earnings_insights: MSFT 1QFY27 reported revenue was $92,279mn (+19% yoy) vs GSe $90,648mn and Street $90,633mn, 2% above both.
Agents and Infra revenue reported $76,795mn (+25% yoy) vs GSe $75,734mn (+23%) and Street $75,679mn. Devices and Consumer reported $15,484mn (-3% yoy) vs GSe $14,913mn and Street $15,026mn.
Adjusted operating income reported $45,915mn (50% margin, +21% yoy) vs GSe $43,977mn and Street $44,006mn. Margin was about 120-124bps above both.
Adjusted EPS reported $4.89 (+27% yoy) vs GSe $4.74 and Street $4.73, 3% above both.
Azure cc growth reported 48% vs GSe 45% and Street 45%. Management guided 2Q Azure cc growth of 49%-50%.
Free cash flow excluding finance leases reported $18,633mn (20% margin, -27% yoy) vs GSe $20,429mn and Street $8,537mn. Capex reported $45,200mn (+30% yoy) vs GSe $52,142mn and Street $51,685mn.

GS quarterly adjusted EPS estimates are $4.84 for 12/26E, $4.90 for 3/27E and $5.10 for 6/27E. The full-year estimates are $19.73 for FY27E, $24.28 for FY28E and $29.87 for FY29E, with FY26 EPS at $17.28.
risk_factors: A longer ramp for internal silicon could limit market share gains or gross margin expansion.
Greater investments in projects outside expectations, such as non-Azure projects.
A more meaningful shift to custom software could hurt the applications business.
Third-party capacity shifting into 2H was delayed, and demand continues to exceed available supply.
vol_and_positioning: The stock was indicated +3% after hours following the print. GS does not cite options or volatility data.
MSFT price performance as of 28 Oct 2026 close: +35.0% over 3 months, +23.7% over 6 months and -2.0% over 12 months. Relative to the S&P 500 it is +29.9%, +14.4% and -12.6% respectively.
